angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 371,504 km at 62.31 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 16.0495 +/- 0.0120 mas (same row, RUWE 1.15): 62.31 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.534 +/- 0.08 solar radii from Esparza-Borges et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2081 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...666A..10E/abstract): 371,504 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.54 +/- 0.08 solar masses from Esparza-Borges et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2081 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...666A..10E/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3800 +/- 100 K from Esparza-Borges et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2081 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...666A..10E/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Esparza-Borges et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2081 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...666A..10E/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2081.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.715, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
